subject: Request: matched consumption audit and retro invoice for May marketplace usage (Optimacloud)
messages:
From: Ben Walsh <ben.walsh@optimacloud.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: finance@optimacloud.com
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Matched consumption audit & retro invoice for May usage (Optimacloud)

Evelyn —

We discovered a discrepancy between the usage we see in our AWS marketplace invoices and the consumption lines that flowed to our financial ledger for May (account OPTC-6789). Our billing team is showing ~2.4% more charged consumption on the marketplace invoice than the metered usage we have recorded in our internal systems. The delta is concentrated on two SKUs that route through the marketplace aggregator (us-east-1).

We need Redwood's help to:
- Run a matched-consumption audit for May 1–31 (line-level).
- Provide the marketplace transaction export (CSV) and any mapping used to convert usage IDs -> invoice lines.
- Confirm whether a retro credit can be issued (credit memo or offset) and whether it will apply to the July invoice or be paid out as a refund.

Attached is a short summary we prepared (optimacloud-usage-mismatch-summary.pdf). We're on a tight closing window for our month-end and request a preliminary response by EOD Tue, July 7 so we can document for procurement.

Who should we loop from procurement/legal if you need PO or entity proof?

Thanks —
Ben Walsh
Head of Finance, Optimacloud
ben.walsh@optimacloud.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: optimacloud-usage-mismatch-summary.pdf (PDF, 240KB)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Ben Walsh <ben.walsh@optimacloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Matched consumption audit & retro invoice for May usage (Optimacloud)

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the summary and the heads-up. We can run a matched-consumption audit; to make sure we return a clean reconciliation we need the following from your side:
- The exact marketplace invoice numbers (may be multiple) you want reconciled.
- Any internal usage CSV you have that maps your customer usage_id -> Optimacloud tenant id.
- Confirmation of the legal entity that should receive a credit/PO (if different from the billing contact).

Tentative plan:
1) Red team (Marissa) will pull the marketplace transaction export and match to our ingestion logs.
2) Karthik will validate mapping for the two SKUs you flagged and look for timestamp drift or duplicative aggregation.
3) We'll produce a reconciliation CSV and proposed credit memo.

Can we schedule a 30-min kickoff Tue Jul 1 at 10:00 PT to align on artifacts and cut-off windows? If that works please confirm and include any procurement contact we should have on the call.

I've attached our internal audit checklist so you know our deliverables.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Customer Finance Ops | Redwood Inference
Evelyn.Hart@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-internal-audit-checklist.docx (DOCX, 85KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Walsh <ben.walsh@optimacloud.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Matched consumption audit & retro invoice for May usage (Optimacloud)

Ben / team —

Following Evelyn's note, we pulled a first-pass export and attached a small reconciliation table (prelim-recon.csv). High-level findings from the initial pass:
- Marketplace invoice INV-202605-OPTC shows 3,214.45 units billed for SKU A-XL; our ingestion logs show 3,146.28 units (difference ~2.16%).
- The delta is concentrated on two short bursts (May 11 22:00–23:30 UTC and May 18 03:15–04:10 UTC) where our aggregator shows duplicated calls from the GCP proxy layer (edge aggregator), likely resulting in double-recorded events for marketplace forwarding.
- There is a timestamp window where our ingestion used rounded minute buckets; marketplace transactions are second-granular. This caused a small alignment mismatch for ~12k tokens worth of usage across the account.

Next steps we propose:
1) We will re-run a per-request reconciliation for the two bursts and produce a locked CSV that includes marketplace_txn_id, marketplace_timestamp, redwood_ingest_id, and matched_flag. (ETA Jul 2 COB).
2) If duplication is confirmed, we will propose a credit memo value and a scope for the retro adjustment (offset vs refund).
3) We need Optimacloud's procurement/legal to confirm that PO-6789 (if you intend to apply credit against a PO) maps to the billed entity.

Quote from Ben's mail below for context:
> We discovered a discrepancy between the usage we see in our AWS marketplace invoices and the consumption lines that flowed to our financial ledger for May (account OPTC-6789).

Attaching the prelim CSV. Will follow up with the per-request extract.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Revenue Operations Analyst | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachment: prelim-recon.csv (CSV, 62KB)

From: Ben Walsh <ben.walsh@optimacloud.com>

Cc: Rita Cho <rita.cho@optimacloud.com>, finance@optimacloud.com
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2026 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Matched consumption audit & retro invoice for May usage (Optimacloud)

Marissa / Evelyn —

Thanks for the quick turn. Rita from procurement is on copy (rita.cho@optimacloud.com) — she'll confirm PO mapping. For transparency I'm attaching PO-6789 and the signed SOW that covers marketplace usage.

We'd prefer a credit memo applied to the July invoice if possible, but we can accept a retro refund if that is Redwood's standard for this class of error. Please confirm which path you recommend after you lock the numbers.

A couple notes:
- The marketplace invoices we have are INV-202605-OPTC and INV-202605-OPTC-2 (both attached in our internal summary).
- Our procurement team requires an audit trail (per-request linkage) for any credit so we can close the month-end.

Ben
Head of Finance, Optimacloud

Attachment: SOW-Marketplace-Usage.pdf (PDF, 1.1MB)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Ben Walsh <ben.walsh@optimacloud.com>, Rita Cho <rita.cho@optimacloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Matched consumption audit & retro invoice for May usage (Optimacloud)

Ben / Rita —

Appreciate the procurement confirmation and the PO. We've completed the per-request reconciliation for the two bursts and confirmed duplication on the aggregator for the windows noted in the preliminary pass. Summary of outcome and next steps: 

1) Reconciliation result: net over-billed consumption for May = 1,545.12 units across the two SKUs (calculated per-request). We include a locked CSV with marketplace_txn_id -> redwood_ingest_id -> delta_flag in the audit bundle (pushed to Drive).
2) Credit path: Redwood will issue a credit memo in the amount of $8,903.42 which can be applied to Optimacloud's July invoice (preferred) or processed as a refund check if you instruct us to do so.
3) Timing & evidence: We will generate the credit memo and the audit bundle (per-request CSV and a short technical note describing the aggregator duplication) by Mon Jul 6 COB. You should have the credit reflected on your July invoice (invoice period starting Jul 1) but we will also provide a credit memo number for your procurement record (PO-6789).
4) Follow-up: Karthik will file a ticket with our edge team to prevent similar duplication on the aggregator routing.

If this approach is acceptable, please confirm and we'll start the credit memo process. If you require an immediate refund instead of an applied credit, note that refunds require CFO-level approval and may take an additional 5–7 business days.

Thanks — we'll also share the Drive folder with the audit artifacts here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDeFgHIjk-audit-bundle

Best,
Evelyn Hart
